messages:
alex: Heads-up — after yesterday's perf run we saw host residency spike when the thin allocator started aggressively evicting lots of small blocks. Need a quick follow-up on heuristics and safe defaults.

maya: What numbers are we looking at? resident % or I/O bandwidth?

samir: Resident set increased ~30% under mixed-batch load. Eviction_count went up and we observed a lot of small DMA migrations; migration bandwidth saturated the PCIe link occasionally.

katie: Is this the eager free-on-host behavior we've been dogfooding? Could be the default policy being too aggressive for our workload mix.

oleg: Confirmed from the profiler: 90% of evicted items were <16KB and fragmentation index crawled up. The allocator ends up creating many tiny free spans, which then get migrated back and forth.

alex: Proposed heuristic: stop immediate evict-on-free. Instead mark freed blocks as reclaimable for a soft-free window (X ms). Only trigger offload if we see memory pressure or sustained growth. This should reduce ping-pong.

maya: Sounds good. How do we define "pressure" though? Free GPU memory % or resident growth rate?

samir: In prior experiments we used resident_delta/sec. Practical composite I suggest: free_mem_pct < 15% OR resident_delta > 20MB/s sustained over 5s. That avoids transient spikes causing churn.

katie: Also gate by allocation size: tiny allocations (<4KB) should not be offloaded at all — the migration overhead outweighs benefit. Put an offload_min_size_bytes threshold.

oleg: Add fragmentation-aware decision: if fragmentation_index > 0.3 prefer internal compaction/merge paths instead of offloading; offloading can worsen fragmentation.

alex: Implementation plan draft: add a pressure-kicker and two knobs: soft_free_window_ms and offload_min_size_bytes. Defaults: 50ms and 4096 bytes. Add metric soft_free_pending_bytes and soft_free_evictions for observability.

maya: We should also add a canary rollout flag: RUNTIME_OFFLOAD_MODE=soft|hard so we can revert quickly.

samir: I'll run an AB perf test in staging (8 streams, mixed seq lengths) comparing hard vs soft. Will measure p50/p95 latency and total migration bytes.

katie: Allocator API change: expose hooks for current_reclaimable_bytes and last_soft_free_time so console can show reclaimable pool and how often we actually evict.

oleg: Edge-case: pinned_staging buffers must bypass soft-free logic (pinned=true tag). Also ensure we don't starve GC: add max_reclaim_age to force eviction after prolonged hold.

samir: Config snippet I'll use for the test:
```
reclaim:
  soft_free_window_ms: 50
  offload_min_size_bytes: 4096
  pressure:
    free_mem_pct_threshold: 15
    resident_growth_mb_s: 20
  max_reclaim_age_ms: 5000
```

katie: Nice. I'll add the hooks and the feature flag in the runtime config and add a unit test around offload_min_size gating.

maya: I'll add Grafana panels: reclaimable bytes, soft_free_pending_count, soft_free_evictions, resident_delta (5s) so we can correlate.

oleg: I'll add stress tests that simulate high tiny-allocation churn to ensure fragmentation path triggers compaction rather than offload.

infra-bot: Deploy preview created: build/rt-1992-softfree. Staging URL: https://staging.redwood/rt/1992

alex: Thanks everyone. Action items: @samir run perf, @maya add metrics dashboard, @katie update allocator API and flag, @oleg add tests. ETA EOD Thursday? We'll reconvene Friday retro to pick defaults.

samir: :thumbsup: starting perf now.

maya: :ok_hand: adding panels.

katie: I'll send a small PR for the API change later today.

oleg: I'll land tests behind feature-flag first.

alex: Closing loop once we have perf signals — plan is to make soft-free default if p95 impact is <2% and migration bytes drop >30%.
